dataset_meta.title: Nakamoto Empirical Rules for Spectral-to-Structural Transition Reasoning
dataset_meta.source: Infrared and Raman Spectra of Inorganic and Coordination Compounds, 6th Ed. by Kazuo Nakamoto (Part A, Chapter 2)

rules.rule: Mutual Exclusion Rule: For centrosymmetric molecules, vibrations that are IR-active are Raman-inactive, and vice versa
molecular_systems: All centrosymmetric point groups (D∞h, D2h, D4h, D6h, Oh, Ih, etc.)
rules.spectral_details: IR and Raman spectra are complementary — bands appear in one but not the other
rules.notes: Key test for presence of inversion center. Exception: violation can occur due to dynamic effects, electronic degeneracy, or symmetry lowering in condensed phases

rules.rule: For linear X₃ (D∞h) molecules: ν₁ (symmetric stretch) is Raman-active only; ν₂ (bend) and ν₃ (asymmetric stretch) are IR-active only
rules.spectral_details: ν₁: Raman only; ν₂, ν₃: IR only

rules.rule: For linear XYZ (C∞v) molecules: all three vibrations (ν₁=ν(XY), ν₂=δ, ν₃=ν(YZ)) are both IR- and Raman-active
rules.spectral_details: All three modes active in both IR and Raman
rules.notes: Loss of inversion center makes all modes active

rules.rule: For bent XY₂ (C2v) and bent XYZ (Cs) molecules: all three normal modes are both IR- and Raman-active
rules.spectral_details: ν₁(sym stretch, A₁), ν₂(bend, A₁), ν₃(asym stretch, B₁) — all active in both

rules.rule: For planar XY₃ (D3h) molecules: ν₁(A₁′) is Raman-active only; ν₂(A₂″) is IR-active only; ν₃(E′) and ν₄(E′) are both IR- and Raman-active
rules.spectral_details: IR shows: ν₂, ν₃, ν₄; Raman shows: ν₁, ν₃, ν₄
rules.notes: Contrast with pyramidal XY₃ (C3v) where all 4 modes are both IR- and Raman-active

rules.rule: For pyramidal XY₃ (C3v) molecules: all four normal modes (ν₁-ν₄) are both IR- and Raman-active
rules.spectral_details: ν₁(A₁, sym str), ν₂(A₁, sym bend), ν₃(E, asym str), ν₄(E, asym bend) — all IR+Raman active

rules.rule: For tetrahedral XY₄ (Td) molecules: ν₁(A₁) and ν₂(E) are Raman-active only; ν₃(F₂) and ν₄(F₂) are both IR- and Raman-active
rules.spectral_details: IR active: ν₃, ν₄; Raman active: ν₁, ν₂, ν₃, ν₄

rules.rule: For square-planar XY₄ (D4h) molecules: ν₁(A₁g), ν₂(B₁g), ν₄(B₂g) are Raman-active; ν₃(A₂u), ν₆(Eu), ν₇(Eu) are IR-active; ν₅(B₂u) is inactive
rules.spectral_details: Raman: ν₁, ν₂, ν₄; IR: ν₃, ν₆, ν₇; ν₅ inactive (observed by INS)
rules.notes: ν₅ can be observed by inelastic neutron scattering (INS)

rules.rule: For octahedral XY₆ (Oh) molecules: ν₁(A₁g), ν₂(Eg), ν₅(F₂g) are Raman-active; ν₃(F₁u), ν₄(F₁u) are IR-active; ν₆(F₂u) is inactive
rules.spectral_details: Raman: ν₁, ν₂, ν₅; IR: ν₃, ν₄; ν₆ inactive (observed by INS)

rules.rule: Icosahedral C₆₀ (Ih): only 4 F₁u vibrations are IR-active; only 2 A_g and 8 H_g vibrations are Raman-active. Mutual exclusion rule holds
Bond order-frequency correlation: Higher bond order → higher vibrational frequency
rules.notes: Bond order, bond distance, bond energy, and vibrational frequency are all correlated. As bond order decreases, distance increases, energy decreases, frequency decreases.

rules.rule: Mass effect within periodic table group: heavier central atom → lower frequency for corresponding vibration
rules.spectral_details: ν ranges: Li₂ 351 → Cs₂ 42 cm⁻¹ (diatomics)
rules.notes: Applies within same group of periodic table. For hydrides: H₂O ~3756 > H₂S ~2627 > H₂Se ~2358 > H₂Te ~2072 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: Across-period frequency trend for hydrides: frequency increases from left to right across periodic table
rules.spectral_details: Increasing frequency trend across period

rules.rule: Halogen frequency trend: M-F > M-Cl > M-Br > M-I for all types of metal-halogen stretching vibrations
molecular_systems: All MXₙ compounds (tetrahedral, octahedral, pyramidal, etc.)
rules.spectral_details: Ratio ν(MBr)/ν(MCl) ≈ 0.76 for ν₃, ≈ 0.61 for ν₁; ν(MI)/ν(MCl) ≈ 0.62 for ν₃, ≈ 0.42 for ν₁
rules.notes: These ratios are remarkably consistent across all compound types and useful for band assignment

rules.rule: Anharmonicity is largest for light molecules and decreases with mass
rules.spectral_details: H₂: xₑωₑ = 117.91 cm⁻¹; Cs₂: xₑωₑ = 0.08 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: For XY₄ tetrahedral molecules: trend ν₃ > ν₁ and ν₄ > ν₂ holds for majority of compounds
rules.spectral_details: Asymmetric stretches (ν₃) are higher than symmetric stretches (ν₁); asymmetric bends (ν₄) higher than symmetric bends (ν₂)

rules.rule: For octahedral XY₆ molecules: stretching frequency order is ν₁ > ν₃ or ν₃ > ν₁ (depends on compound); bending order is ν₄ > ν₅ > ν₆ in most cases
rules.spectral_details: ν₁ > ν₃ for many but not all compounds; ν₄ > ν₅ > ν₆ for bending modes

rules.rule: For trigonal-bipyramidal XY₅: equatorial stretching frequencies > axial stretching frequencies. Trend: ν₅ > ν₃ > ν₁ > ν₂
rules.spectral_details: ν₅ (asym equatorial stretch) > ν₃ (asym axial stretch) > ν₁ (sym equatorial) > ν₂ (sym axial)
rules.notes: Equatorial bonds are stronger than axial bonds in TBP structures

rules.rule: For tetragonal-pyramidal XY₅: axial stretching frequency (ν₁) is higher than equatorial stretching frequencies (ν₂, ν₄, ν₇) — opposite to TBP trend
rules.spectral_details: ν₁(axial) > ν₂, ν₄, ν₇(equatorial)

rules.rule: For diatomic XY molecules: frequency decreases when bonding electrons are removed; increases when antibonding electrons are removed
rules.spectral_details: Bonding MO removal: ν decreases; Antibonding MO removal: ν increases
rules.notes: Interpretable via simple molecular orbital theory

rules.rule: Distinguishing linear vs bent XY₂: ν₁ is IR-inactive for linear (D∞h) but IR-active for bent (C2v). In practice, many bent molecules have bond angles 95-170°
molecular_systems: XY₂ metal halides: BeF₂(linear), CaF₂(bent), SrF₂(bent), BaF₂(bent)
rules.spectral_details: Linear: ν₁ IR-inactive, ν₂+ν₃ IR-active; Bent: ν₁+ν₂+ν₃ all IR-active
rules.notes: Caution: matrix effects can change structure (NiCl₂ is linear in Ar but bent ~130° in N₂ matrices)

rules.rule: Distinguishing pyramidal (C3v) vs planar (D3h) XY₃: pyramidal shows 2 stretching bands (ν₁ A₁ + ν₃ E) in IR; planar shows 1 stretching band (ν₃ E′) in IR
rules.spectral_details: Pyramidal: both ν₁(sym) and ν₃(asym) IR-active; Planar: only ν₃(E′) IR-active, ν₁(A₁′) Raman only
rules.notes: This is the key spectroscopic test for tautomerism (e.g., SO₃²⁻ pyramidal vs SO₃ planar)

rules.rule: Distinguishing trigonal-bipyramidal (D3h) vs tetragonal-pyramidal (C4v) XY₅: TBP has 2 IR-active stretches; TP has 3 IR-active stretches
rules.spectral_details: TBP: ν₃(A₂″) and ν₅(E′) IR-active; TP: ν₁(A₁), ν₂(A₁), ν₇(E) IR-active
rules.notes: In practice, band overlapping can make counting difficult. Additional criterion: TBP has equatorial > axial frequency; TP has axial > equatorial

rules.rule: Bond angle calculation in YXY from isotopic frequency ratio: use ν₃/ν₃′ ratio with isotopic substitution at X
rules.spectral_details: ν̃₃′/ν̃₃ = √[(M_X + M_X′ + M_Y(1-cosα))/(M_X′(M_X + M_Y(1-cosα)))]
rules.notes: Example: NiF₂ bond angle calculated as 154-167° from isotopic data

rules.rule: For X₂Y₄ (ethane-like) molecules: trans (C2h) shows 6 IR fundamentals, gauche (C2) shows 12 IR fundamentals
rules.spectral_details: Counting IR-active fundamentals distinguishes conformers
rules.notes: N₂H₄ is pure gauche in all states; P₂H₄ is gauche in gas but trans in solid

rules.rule: For X₂Y₄ (B₂X₄-type) molecules: D2h (planar) vs D2d (staggered) distinguished by number of IR fundamentals: 8 for D2, 5 for D2d
rules.spectral_details: D2h: mutual exclusion rule holds (inversion center); D2d: no inversion center
rules.notes: B₂F₄ and B₂Cl₄ are staggered in gas/liquid, planar in solid; B₂Br₄ staggered in all phases

rules.rule: Pentagonal-planar XY₅ (D5h) structure confirmed by only 3 IR-active and 3 Raman-active bands, vs many more for TBP or TP alternatives
rules.spectral_details: XeF₅⁻: IR=3 bands, Raman=3 bands (ν₁ 502, ν₃ 423, ν₄ 377 cm⁻¹)

rules.rule: Cis/trans isomer distinction in octahedral XY₄Z₂: trans (D4h) gives 3 XY stretches (A1g+B1g+Eu) with Eu IR-active only; cis (C2v) gives 4 XY stretches (2A1+B1+B2) all IR+Raman active
rules.spectral_details: Trans: fewer bands, mutual exclusion; Cis: more bands, all active

rules.rule: O-H stretching: free OH ~3600-3700 cm⁻¹; H-bonded OH ~3400-3200 cm⁻¹ (broad); O-H bending ~1600-1650 cm⁻¹
rules.notes: H-bonding lowers ν(OH) stretch and raises δ(OH) bend. Liquid water shows isosbestic point at 3403 cm⁻¹ in Raman

rules.rule: N-H stretching: ~3300-3400 cm⁻¹ (NH₃ gas: ν₁ 3414, ν₃ 3336 cm⁻¹); N-H bending: ~1600-1650 cm⁻¹ (ν₂), ~930-970 cm⁻¹ (ν₄)
rules.spectral_details: NH₃ gas: ν₁ 3414, ν₂ 1627.5/931.6 (inversion doublet), ν₃ 3337, ν₄ 968 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: C-H stretching: ~2900-3100 cm⁻¹; C-H bending: ~1300-1500 cm⁻¹
rules.spectral_details: CH₄: ν₁ 2917, ν₂ 1534, ν₃ 3019, ν₄ 1306 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: Si-H stretching: ~2100-2200 cm⁻¹; Si-H bending: ~900-1000 cm⁻¹
rules.spectral_details: SiH₄: ν₁ 2180, ν₂ 970, ν₃ 2183, ν₄ 910 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: S-H stretching: ~2550-2620 cm⁻¹; S-H bending: ~1180 cm⁻¹
rules.spectral_details: H₂S gas: ν₁ 2615, ν₂ 1183, ν₃ 2627 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: B-H terminal stretching: ~2500-2600 cm⁻¹; B-H bridging stretching: ~2100-2200 cm⁻¹
rules.spectral_details: Terminal ν(BH): 2500-2600 cm⁻¹; Bridging ν(BH): 2100-2200 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: P-H stretching: ~2300-2420 cm⁻¹ (PH₃: ν₁ 2327, ν₃ 2421 cm⁻¹)
rules.spectral_details: PH₃: ν₂ 992/990 (inversion), ν₄ 1121 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: N≡N (triple bond) stretching: ~2300-2400 cm⁻¹ (N₂: 2359, N₂⁺: 2207 cm⁻¹); N=N (double): ~1550 cm⁻¹; N-N (single): ~1000 cm⁻¹
rules.spectral_details: N≡N: ~2300-2400; N=N: ~1550; N-N: ~1000 cm⁻¹ (approximate ranges)

rules.rule: C≡N (nitrile) stretching: ~2100-2250 cm⁻¹; C≡P stretching: ~1540-1565 cm⁻¹
rules.spectral_details: HCN: ν₁ 3311, ν₂ 712, ν₃ 2097 cm⁻¹; CH₃C≡P: ~1543-1565 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: C≡C (triple bond) stretching: ~1700-2200 cm⁻¹ (C₂: ~1757 cm⁻¹ matrix); C=C (double): ~1500-1680 cm⁻¹; C-C (single): ~1000-1300 cm⁻¹
rules.spectral_details: C₂: 1757-1845 cm⁻¹; C₆₀ A_g(2): 1469 cm⁻¹; Diamond: 1332 cm⁻¹; Graphite: 1575 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: C=O (carbonyl) stretching: ~1700 cm⁻¹ for normal ketones; lower (~1600 cm⁻¹ or below) for aromatic/unsaturated systems
rules.spectral_details: CO₂: ν₃ 2349 cm⁻¹ (antisym); Normal ketones ~1700 cm⁻¹; Aromatic CₙOₙ²⁻ rings: <1600 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: U=O (uranyl) stretching: ~860-960 cm⁻¹; relationship with U=O distance: R = 9141(ν̃₃)⁻²/³ + 80.4 (in pm)
rules.spectral_details: UO₂²⁺ ν₃: ~950 cm⁻¹; PuO₂²⁺ ν₃: 962 cm⁻¹; AmO₂²⁺ ν₃: 939 cm⁻¹; (U⁴VO₂)²⁺ ν₃: 895 → (U⁵VO₂)⁺: 770 cm⁻¹ on reduction

rules.rule: SiO₄ tetrahedra in silicates: ν₁(A₁) 750-830 cm⁻¹; ν₂(E) 300-400 cm⁻¹; ν₃(F₂) 800-1000 cm⁻¹; ν₄(F₂) 450-600 cm⁻¹
rules.spectral_details: Distinguish structural units by ν(Si-O): 4 terminal O ~850, 3 terminal ~900, 2 terminal ~950-1000, 1 terminal ~1050-1100 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: Nitrosyl (NO) stretching: strongly dependent on charge. NO⁺ ~2273, NO ~1880, NO⁻ ~1358-1374, (NO)₂⁻ ~886 cm⁻¹
rules.spectral_details: NO⁺(solid): 2273; NO(matrix): 1880; NO⁻: 1358-1374 (matrix); (NO)₂⁻: 886 cm⁻¹ (matrix)

rules.rule: Fullerene C₆₀ characteristic modes: IR-active at 1428, 1182, 577, 527 cm⁻¹; Raman-active pentagonal pinching mode (A_g) at 1469 cm⁻¹, radial breathing (A_g) at 496 cm⁻¹
rules.spectral_details: Doping shifts A_g(2) from 1469 → 1452 (K₃C₆₀), 1448 (Rb₃C₆₀) cm⁻¹. Each electron transferred shifts ~7 cm⁻¹ down

rules.rule: Carbon nanotube radial breathing mode (RBM): ν(RBM) is inversely proportional to tube diameter. ν ~ 186 cm⁻¹ for d ~ 1.4 nm
rules.spectral_details: ν(RBM) = A/d + B (A ~234 cm⁻¹·nm). Strong resonance enhancement at specific excitation wavelengths

rules.rule: Higher oxidation state of central atom → higher stretching frequency for the same molecular type
rules.spectral_details: VF₆⁻: ν₁ 676, ν₃ 646; VF₆²⁻: ν₁ 584, ν₃ 578; VF₆³⁻: ν₁ 533, ν₃ 511 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: Fe oxidation state effect on Fe-X frequency: ν(FeX₄⁻) / ν(FeX₄²⁻) ≈ 1.32 for X=Cl, Br
rules.spectral_details: ν₃(FeCl₄⁻) ~378, ν₃(FeCl₄²⁻) ~286 cm⁻¹; ratio ≈ 1.32

rules.rule: For tetrahedral oxoanions MO₄ⁿ⁻: ν₁/ν₃ ratio increases with (1) increasing negative charge for same central atom, (2) increasing mass of central atom for same charge, (3) increasing negative charge for isoelectronic ions
rules.spectral_details: ν₁/ν₃ increases systematically with charge and mass
rules.notes: Very useful for making correct ν₁/ν₃ assignments in tetraoxoanions

rules.rule: Removing bonding electrons → frequency decrease; removing antibonding electrons → frequency increase (diatomics)
rules.spectral_details: N₂: losing bonding e⁻ decreases ν; O₂: losing antibonding e⁻ increases ν

rules.rule: For NH₄⁺ in ammonium halides: ν(NH₄⁺) decreases and δ(NH₄⁺) increases as N-H···X hydrogen bond weakens in order X = F > Cl > Br > I
rules.spectral_details: ν(NH) becomes lower; δ(NH) becomes higher from F to I

rules.rule: In BH₄⁻, GaH₄⁻, AlH₄⁻ series (group IIIB): unusual trend ν₁(BH₄⁻ 2270) > ν₁(GaH₄⁻ 1807) > ν₁(AlH₄⁻ 1757 cm⁻¹) — does not follow simple mass trend
rules.spectral_details: ν₁: BH₄⁻ 2270 > GaH₄⁻ 1807 > AlH₄⁻ 1757 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: Mixed halogen systems: stretching frequencies are additive and characteristic. For mixed complexes, ratios ν(MBr)/ν(MCl) ≈ 0.76 and ν(MI)/ν(MCl) ≈ 0.62 for ν₃
rules.spectral_details: Average ratios across many compounds provide reliable band assignment guide

rules.rule: For SiFₙCl₄₋ₙ, SiClₙBr₄₋ₙ series: each stretching vibration appears at characteristic frequency determined by the specific M-X bond (e.g., SiF 910, SiCl 587, SiBr 486, SiI 333 cm⁻¹ in SiFClBrI)
rules.spectral_details: SiF 910, SiCl 587, SiBr 486, SiI 333 cm⁻¹ in SiFClBrI

rules.rule: Terminal vs bridging M-X stretching: terminal frequencies are higher than bridging frequencies. Ratio ν(bridge)/ν(terminal) ranges from 0.74 to 0.61
rules.spectral_details: Terminal stretching ~1.3-1.6× bridging stretching frequencies

rules.rule: M-O-M bridge angle correlation: νₐ(MO) is at least 215 cm⁻¹ higher than νₛ(MO). This separation increases as M-O-M angle increases
rules.spectral_details: For V₂O₇: Δ = [(νₐ-νₛ)/(νₐ+νₛ)]×100 = -38.79 + 0.39α (where α is M-O-M angle)

rules.rule: Isotope shifts in diatomic molecules: ν(HX)/ν(DX) ≈ √2 ≈ 1.414 for hydrides/deuterides
molecular_systems: H/D isotopic pairs in all molecular types
rules.notes: Isotope substitution is the most powerful tool for band assignment

rules.rule: Chlorine isotope pattern in tetrahedral and octahedral MClₙ compounds: 5-peak pattern from ³⁵Cl/³⁷Cl (75.4%/24.6%) mixture. Isotope shift per mass unit ≈ 3.8 cm⁻¹ for Cl in MCl₄
rules.spectral_details: 5-peak pattern with approximately known relative intensities from statistical distribution
rules.notes: For SnCl₄ with 10 Sn isotopes, 50 bands expected. Using isotopically pure ¹¹⁶SnCl₄ gives clean 5-peak Cl pattern

rules.rule: ¹⁰B/¹¹B isotope effect (natural 19.8%/80.2%): useful for band assignment in boron compounds
rules.spectral_details: B-isotope shifts help identify B-containing modes. Boron isotopes produce characteristic splitting patterns

rules.rule: Carbon isotope scrambling (¹²C/¹³C) for determining structure: number of isotopomer peaks in IR identifies molecular geometry (linear vs cyclic vs TBP)
rules.spectral_details: C₅ linear: 20 isotopomer peaks; C₅ TBP: 12 peaks; C₅ cyclic: 8 peaks. Linear confirmed by 20 observed peaks

rules.rule: ²³⁵U/²³⁸U isotope shift in UF₆: only 0.604 cm⁻¹. High-resolution cold-jet technique required to resolve
rules.spectral_details: ²³⁵UF₆ Q-branch lies between R(5) and R(6) of ²³⁸UF₆. Used for laser isotope separation

rules.rule: Hydrogen bonding: lowers X-H stretching frequency (broadens band), raises X-H bending frequency
rules.spectral_details: H₂O: gas ν₁ 3657→liquid 3450→ice 3400 cm⁻¹ (stretch decreases); δ: gas 1595→liquid 1640→ice 1620 cm⁻¹ (bend increases)

rules.rule: Matrix effects: vibrational frequencies differ depending on matrix gas (Ne, Ar, Kr, N₂). Structure may also change (e.g., NiCl₂ linear in Ar, bent ~130° in N₂)
rules.spectral_details: CaF₂ bond angle: 139° (Kr) → 143° (Ne) → 156° (N₂ matrix)
rules.notes: Structural data from matrix must be interpreted with caution

rules.rule: Pressure effects: high pressure can distort tetrahedral ions toward square-planar; increase stretching frequencies due to bond shortening
rules.spectral_details: ν(Re-Re) at 15 GPa: 272 → 357 cm⁻¹ (shift +85 cm⁻¹)

rules.rule: Solution vs solid state: ν₁ and ν₃ often too close in Raman spectra of solids but separate in solution. ν₂ and ν₄ may merge
rules.spectral_details: Raman: ν₂ stronger than ν₄ in MO₄ⁿ⁻; ν₄ often hidden by ν₂

rules.rule: Site symmetry lowering in crystalline state: degenerate vibrations (ν₃, ν₄) can split into two or three components due to crystal field effects
rules.spectral_details: Splitting magnitude provides information about site symmetry

rules.rule: Temperature-dependent isomer equilibria: shifts between different molecular structures observable via frequency changes (e.g., XeF₆ three electronic isomers)
molecular_systems: N₂O₄ (planar D2h ↔ twisted D2d ↔ iso form)
rules.spectral_details: XeF₆ IR stretching bands change with temperature due to shift in isomer equilibrium

rules.rule: Force constant-bond distance correlation for U=O: Jones derived relationship between U=O stretching force constant and U=O distance
rules.spectral_details: U=O distance R(pm) = 9141(ν̃₃)⁻²/³ + 80.4, or R = 10650(ν̃₁)⁻²/³ + 57.5

rules.rule: Empirical relationship between νₐ(M-Cl) and M-Cl distance in planar Pt(II) and Pd(II) complexes: [νₐ(M-Cl)]² = P/(R(M-Cl)-1.6)³
rules.spectral_details: P = 38988 for Pt(II), 41440 for Pd(II); R in Å, ν in cm⁻¹

rules.rule: Trend within X₄⁴⁻ (tetrahedral) and isoelectronic Y₄: ν(X₄⁴⁻)/ν(Y₄) ≈ 0.77
rules.spectral_details: Based on this ratio, Pb₄⁴⁻ predicted: ν₁ 115, ν₂ 69, ν₃ 93 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: Metal-oxygen stretching force constants in M₆O₁₉⁸⁻ clusters: ratio of terminal:bridging:central ≈ 6:3:1
rules.spectral_details: Terminal ~5.66, bridging ~2.92, central ~0.91 mdyn/Å

rules.rule: Metal-metal stretching in clusters: strong Raman bands at low frequencies (100-400 cm⁻¹). Under resonance conditions, overtones of ν(M-M) dominate spectra
rules.spectral_details: ν(Re-Re): F 320, Cl 272, Br 277, I 258 cm⁻¹ (irregular halogen dependence)

rules.rule: M-M stretching in excited electronic state can be lower (bonding→antibonding excitation) or higher (antibonding→bonding excitation) than ground state
rules.spectral_details: Re₂Cl₈²⁻: ν(Re-Re) ground 272 → excited 204 cm⁻¹ (electron promoted from bonding d to antibonding d*)

rules.rule: Metal carbonyl ν(CO) vibrations: terminal CO ~2000-2130 cm⁻¹; bridging CO ~1800-1860 cm⁻¹
rules.spectral_details: Terminal ν(CO): ~2000-2130; Bridging ν(CO): ~1800-1860 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: Dioxygen (O₂) ligand vibrations depend on charge state: O₂⁺ ~1876, O₂ ~1580, O₂⁻ ~1094, O₂²⁻ ~791/736 cm⁻¹. Used to identify ligand type in coordination compounds
B₆X₆²⁻ ions (Oh symmetry): B-B vibrations are insensitive to halogen; B-X vibrations are sensitive. Only 4 IR-active (F₁u) and 3 Raman-active (A₁g+E_g+F₂g) for B₆ skeleton
rules.spectral_details: B-B modes relatively constant, B-X modes shift with halogen (Cl→Br→I)

rules.rule: For icosahedral B₁₂X₁₂²⁻ (Ih): only 3 F₁u IR-active, and only 2 A_g + 4 H_g Raman-active out of 66 normal modes
rules.spectral_details: Very simple IR/Raman spectra despite 24 atoms due to extremely high symmetry

rules.rule: Small carbon clusters Cₙ (n=2-13): neutral clusters are predominantly linear (except C₆ which can be cyclic). Cₙ⁻ anions have markedly lower frequencies than neutrals
molecular_systems: C₃, C₄, C₅, C₆, C₇, C₈, C₉, C₁₁, C₁₃
rules.spectral_details: C₅⁻ stretching is 332 cm⁻¹ lower than C₅; C₇⁻ is 394 cm⁻¹ lower than C₇

rules.rule: Sulfur clusters Sₙ (n=6-12): neutral molecules take puckered ring structures; anions Sₙ²⁻ (n=4-6) take open-chain structures
rules.spectral_details: Neutral: ring (puckered); Anions: open chain

rules.rule: Inversion doubling in pyramidal XH₃: each vibrational level splits into positive and negative components. Transitions between different signs are IR-allowed; same sign are Raman-allowed
rules.spectral_details: NH₃ ground state inversion splitting: ~0.79 cm⁻¹ (microwave). ν₂: 931.6/968.1 cm⁻¹ doublet

rules.rule: Fermi resonance: when a fundamental and overtone/combination have similar frequencies and same symmetry, they mix and split. The higher-frequency band gains intensity
rules.spectral_details: CO₂: ν₁ expected ~1337 but 2ν₂(∼1337) Fermi resonance gives bands at 1285 and 1388 cm⁻¹
rules.notes: Important consideration in band assignment. The unperturbed frequency can be calculated

rules.rule: Resonance Raman (RR) enhancement: when excitation wavelength matches electronic absorption, vibrational modes coupled to the electronic transition are strongly enhanced, producing overtone progressions
rules.spectral_details: RR shows nν₁ (n=1-9) progressions. Mode selectivity reveals which bonds are involved in electronic transition

rules.rule: Jahn-Teller effect in octahedral d¹ and d² hexafluorides: combination bands (ν₁+ν₃) and (ν₂+ν₃) show anomalous broadening
rules.spectral_details: Broadening of (ν₂+ν₃) and (ν₁+ν₃) combination bands in IR; no splitting of fundamentals

rules.rule: Anomalous polarization in resonance Raman: for octahedral d⁵ ions (e.g., IrCl₆²⁻), all Raman bands can show anomalous polarization due to electronic degeneracy
rules.spectral_details: Depolarization ratios deviate from normal values. Antisymmetric part of Raman tensor from d⁵ electronic degeneracy

rules.rule: Electronic structure effect on ν₃ in octahedral [MCl₆]³⁻: occupation of antibonding e_g orbitals drastically lowers ν₃ (Fe³⁺ d⁵ < Cr³⁺ d³)
rules.spectral_details: ν₃: Cr³⁺ 315 > Mn³⁺ 342 (J-T distorted, extra splitting) > Fe³⁺ 248 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: Group frequency charts provide characteristic absorption regions for common functional groups in phosphorus, sulfur, and boron compounds
rules.spectral_details: See Appendix VIII of Nakamoto for complete group frequency charts

rules.rule: For pyramidal XY₃ halogeno compounds: trend ν₁ > ν₃ and ν₂ > ν₄ (opposite to neutral XH₃ molecules where ν₃ > ν₁ and ν₄ > ν₂)
rules.spectral_details: Halogeno: ν₁ > ν₃, ν₂ > ν₄; Hydrides: ν₃ > ν₁, ν₄ > ν₂

rules.rule: In XY₂ triatomic molecules: trend ν₃ > ν₁ holds for majority; exceptions occur for some bent molecules
rules.spectral_details: ν₃ (asymmetric stretch) usually higher than ν₁ (symmetric stretch)

rules.rule: For octahedral XY₆: ν₁(AlF₆³⁻ 541) > ν₁(GaF₆³⁻ 535) > ν₁(InF₆³⁻ 497) > ν₁(TlF₆³⁻ 478) — ν₁ shows force constant trend directly since central atom is stationary in this mode
rules.spectral_details: ν₁ trend: Al > Ga > In > Tl (force constant dominance); ν₃ trend: same order (mass + force constant combined)

rules.rule: For tetrahedral MO₄ⁿ⁻ series: ν₁ and ν₃ trends depend on central atom, charge, and period. The n₁/n₃ ratio is diagnostic for correct assignment
rules.spectral_details: ν₁/ν₃ increases with negative charge and central atom mass

rules.rule: Distinction between cis/trans isomers in X₂Y₂ molecules: cis (C2v) vs trans (C2h). ν₆ vibration is IR-inactive and Raman-depolarized in planar but IR-active and Raman-polarized in nonplanar
rules.spectral_details: ν₆: IR and Raman behavior distinguishes cis-planar (C2v), trans-planar (C2h), and nonplanar (C2)

rules.rule: Planar (D2h) vs twisted (D2) X₂H₄: D2h has IR/Raman mutual exclusion; D2 (nonplanar) does not
rules.spectral_details: Selection rule test: D2h → inversion center → mutual exclusion; D2 → no inversion center

rules.rule: D3h (staggered) vs D3h′ (eclipsed) for ethane-like X₂Y₆: D3d has E_u IR-active + E_g Raman-active; D3h has E′ both IR and Raman active
rules.spectral_details: Si₂Cl₆ controversy: D3d vs D3h resolved by observing ν₈ and ν₉ weakly in Raman (violation for D3d, allowed for D3h′/G₃₆)

rules.rule: In M₂X₉ (triple-bridged) clusters: terminal stretching ~340-430 cm⁻¹; bridging stretching ~200-320 cm⁻¹. Terminal/bridging ratio ~1.3-1.5
rules.spectral_details: Terminal and bridging mode frequencies are characteristic and well-separated

rules.rule: In M₂X₁₀ (edge-sharing bioctahedra): terminal vibrations: 320-370 cm⁻¹; bridging vibrations: 250-280 cm⁻¹
rules.spectral_details: Terminal/bridging mode separation useful for structure confirmation

rules.rule: Adduct formation with HF: H-bonded vs anti-H-bonded complexes can be distinguished by ν(HF) shifts. UF₆-HF at 3848 cm⁻¹; UF₆-FH at 3903 cm⁻¹
rules.spectral_details: H-bonded: HF stretch lower; anti-H-bonded: HF stretch higher (closer to free HF)

rules.rule: Octahedral metal clusters [M₆X₈Y₆]²⁻ (M=Mo, W): ν(M-M) ~200-300 cm⁻¹, force constant 1.2-1.5 mdyn/Å. Two Raman-active (A₁g, E_g) and one IR-active (F₁u) M-M modes
rules.spectral_details: ν(Mo-Mo) below 300 cm⁻¹; force constants 1.2-1.5 mdyn/Å

rules.rule: Nb₆Cl₁₂ cluster: ν(Nb-Nb) assigned at ~140 cm⁻¹. Force constant < 0.3 mdyn/Å — much weaker than Mo/W clusters
rules.spectral_details: ν(M-M) very low; may be too low to observe in some cases

rules.rule: Diamond Raman: single sharp band at 1332 cm⁻¹ (F₂g, triply degenerate). Used as pressure sensor in diamond anvil cells. Type I vs II diamond distinguished by IR absorption
rules.spectral_details: Raman: 1332 cm⁻¹; IR: type I ~2000 + ~1200 cm⁻¹; type II ~2000 cm⁻¹ only

rules.rule: Graphite Raman: single band at 1575 cm⁻¹ (E₂g). No IR bands (inactive due to D6h symmetry)
rules.spectral_details: Raman: 1575 cm⁻¹; IR: none (intersheet interaction negligible for vibrational analysis)

rules.rule: Small silicon clusters Siₙ: counting Raman-active fundamentals identifies geometry (e.g., Si₄ planar rhombus D2h: 3 Raman; Si₆ distorted octahedron D4h: 5 Raman; Si₇ pentagonal bipyramid D5h: 5 Raman)
rules.spectral_details: Compare observed #Raman bands with predicted for each candidate geometry

rules.rule: Cation effect on anion structure: smaller alkali metal cations favor type II (symmetric) H-bonded anions; larger cations prefer type I (asymmetric). Eg: [FHCl]⁻ ions
rules.spectral_details: Type I: ν₃(mainly ν(HF)) ~2500 cm⁻¹; Type II (symmetric): ν₃ ~933 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: Raman intensity ordering in octahedral XY₆: normally I(ν₁) > I(ν₂) > I(ν₅). Exception: d⁶ ions (Pt, Pd hexahalides) show I(ν₂) > I(ν₁) due to nonbonding d electrons
rules.spectral_details: Normal: I(ν₁) > I(ν₂) > I(ν₅); Anomalous d⁶: I(ν₂) > I(ν₁)

rules.rule: Trigonal-bipyramidal structure has stronger equatorial bonds than axial bonds (confirmed by force constant calculations). Tetragonal-pyramidal has stronger axial bond
rules.spectral_details: TBP: equatorial force constant > axial; TP: axial > equatorial

Polymeric nitrogen (cubic gauche) at high pressure: ν(N-N) at 840 cm⁻¹ vs molecular N₂ at 2400 cm⁻¹ — dramatic shift indicates phase change from triple-bonded N₂ to single-bonded polymeric N
rules.spectral_details: Molecular N₂: ~2400 cm⁻¹; Polymeric N (single bonds): ~840 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: For XH₄⁺ series (group V onium ions): ν(NH₄⁺ 3145) > ν(PH₄⁺ 2366) > ν(AsH₄⁺ 2341) > ν(SbH₄⁺ 2061 cm⁻¹) — decreases with central atom mass

rules.rule: Endohedral fullerene symmetry: violation of mutual exclusion rule and more IR/Raman bands than predicted for Ih symmetry indicates lowering due to metal-cage interaction

rules.rule: Free internal rotation in ethane-like X₂Y₆: low barrier leads to G₃₆ dynamic group symmetry, allowing normally IR-inactive modes to appear weakly in Raman

rules.spectral_details: Molecular N≡N: ~2400 cm⁻¹; Polymeric N-N: ~840 cm⁻¹ (Raman)

rules.rule: Graphite: single Raman band at 1575 cm⁻¹ (E₂g). No IR bands (D6h symmetry). ν(RBM) of SWNT ~186 cm⁻¹ for d~1.4 nm, inversely proportional to diameter
rules.spectral_details: Graphite Raman: 1575 cm⁻¹. SWNT RBM: ν ~ 234/d (nm⁻¹)

rules.rule: Nitrile imide CBS: ν(CBS) at 1800 cm⁻¹. Carbon suboxide C₃O₂: νₐ(C=O) ~2290 cm⁻¹. Carbon oxide anions CₙOₙ²⁻: ν(C=O) below 1600 cm⁻¹ (aromatic ring stabilization)
rules.spectral_details: ν(CBS): 1800; normal C=O: ~1700; aromatic CₙOₙ²⁻: <1600 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: Hydrogen bifluoride [F-H-F]⁻: linear symmetric. ν₃(asym stretch) ~1450, ν₂(bend) ~1233, ν₁(sym stretch) ~596-603 cm⁻¹. [F-H-Cl]⁻ type I (asym): ν₃ ~2500, type II (sym): ν₃ ~933 cm⁻¹
rules.spectral_details: Type I (asymmetric H): ν₃ ~2500; Type II (symmetric H): ν₃ ~933 cm⁻¹; [FHF]⁻: ν₁ 596-603, ν₂ 1233, ν₃ 1450 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: Sulfur-nitrogen heterocycles: S₂N₂ ν(SN) ~880-930 cm⁻¹. Tetrasulfur tetranitride S₄N₄ (D2d): cage structure, ν(SN) ~700-900, ν(SS) ~300-500 cm⁻¹
rules.spectral_details: (SNH)₄ (C4v): SN stretch 800-700, δ(SNH) ~1350, ν(NH) ~3250 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: ν(P-O-P) bridge in pyrophosphates: νₐ(P-O-P) ~915, νₛ ~730, δ ~94 cm⁻¹. Also applicable to As₂O₇⁴⁻, S₂O₇²⁻, V₂O₇⁴⁻, Cr₂O₇²⁻ with systematic shifts
rules.spectral_details: νₐ(P-O-P): 915; νₛ: 730; δ: 94 cm⁻¹. Other M₂O₇: systematic variations

rules.rule: AlO₄ vibrations in aluminosilicates: ν(Al-O) ~750-650 cm⁻¹. Framework silicates (zeolites): characteristic Al-O + Si-O combined bands in this region
rules.spectral_details: ν(Al-O): 750-650 cm⁻¹ (in addition to SiO₄ bands)

rules.rule: Diazene N₂H₂: cis form ν(N-H) 3116/3025, δ 1347/1304 cm⁻¹; trans form ν(N-H) 3109, δ 1333 cm⁻¹. N₂F₂: cis ν(N=N) 1525, ν(N-F) 896/952; trans ν(N=N) 1522, ν(N-F) 1010/990 cm⁻¹
H₂O₂: ν(OH) 3607/3608, ν(OO) 1394, δ(HOO) 864/1266, torsion 317 cm⁻¹. H₂O₂ nonplanar C2 with dihedral ~90°
C₃O₂ (carbon suboxide): linear O=C=C=C=O, ν₃(C=O) ~2290 cm⁻¹. C₆₀Br₂₄: ν(C=C) IR at 1688, 1641, 1610 cm⁻¹; Raman at 1690, 1675, 1654, 1631, 1607 cm⁻¹
Sc-N stretching in Sc₃N@C₈₀: νₐ(E′) 599, νₛ(A₁′) 411, δ(E′) 210 cm⁻¹ (Raman). νₐ ~597 cm⁻¹ (IR). On Sc→Y substitution: shifts to 707, 429, 194 cm⁻¹
rules.spectral_details: νₐ: 599→707; νₛ: 411→429; δ: 210→194 cm⁻¹ (Sc→Y substitution)

rules.rule: Metal-cage vibrations in endohedral fullerenes: Sc₂@C₈₄ ν(Sc-C) ~250 cm⁻¹; Raman cage-modes at 133, 108, 78, 48 cm⁻¹ for Sc₃N@C₈₀ (translational/rotational modes)
rules.spectral_details: Sc-C stretch ~250, δ ~140-70 cm⁻¹; Eu@C₇₄ cage-mode 123 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: SiC (silicon carbide) clusters: SiC₄ linear ~2038 cm⁻¹; Si₂C₂ rhombic ν(Si-C) ~800-1000; Si₃C linear; Si₃C₂ rhomboidal; Si₂C₃ pentagonal. Si₅H₁₀ and Si₆H₁₂ silanes: nonplanar SiH₂ rings
rules.spectral_details: SiC₄: ~2038; Si₂C₂: ν(Si-C) 800-1000 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: ν(OF) in FOOF (dioxygen difluoride): ν(O-F) at 376/586 cm⁻¹, ν(O-O) ~1500 cm⁻¹. ν(Cl-O) in ClO₂: ν₁ 945, ν₂ 449, ν₃ 1108 cm⁻¹. BrO₂: ν₁ 796, ν₂ 317, ν₃ 845 cm⁻¹
rules.spectral_details: ClO₂: ν₁ 945, ν₂ 449, ν₃ 1108; BrO₂: ν₁ 796, ν₂ 317, ν₃ 845 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: O₃ (ozone): ν₁ 1104, ν₂ 700, ν₃ 1040 cm⁻¹. O₃⁻ (ozonide): ν₁ 1020, ν₂ 620, ν₃ 816 cm⁻¹ (bent C2v). All three modes IR+Raman active
rules.spectral_details: O₃: ν₁ 1104, ν₂ 700, ν₃ 1040 cm⁻¹; O₃⁻: ν₁ 1020, ν₂ 620, ν₃ 816 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: HArF (first neutral argon compound): ν(H-Ar) 1969.5, δ(H-Ar-F) 687.0, ν(Ar-F) 435.7 cm⁻¹ (Ar matrix, 7.5K). HKrF: ν(H-Kr) 1950, ν(Kr-F) 415 cm⁻¹
SnX₃⁻ (trigonal pyramidal): SnCl₃⁻: ν₁ 297, ν₂ 130, ν₃ 256, ν₄ 104; SnBr₃⁻: ν₁ 205, ν₂ 82, ν₃ 180, ν₄ 65; SnI₃⁻: ν₁ 162, ν₂ 61, ν₃ 148, ν₄ 48 cm⁻¹
C₃⁺ cyclopropenium: ν(C-C) at 1790 and 1315, ν(C-Cl) at 733 and 458 cm⁻¹. In-plane bending 600 and 160, out-of-plane 524 and 190 cm⁻¹
Polyiodide anions: I₃⁻ ν₁ 125-116, ν₂ 56-42, ν₃ ~125 cm⁻¹; I₅⁻ ν(I-I) ~178/166, νₐ I₃ units ~152, νₛ ~118 cm⁻¹; I₂ ν ~213 cm⁻¹. Vibrations strongly depend on cation
rules.spectral_details: I₃⁻: ν₁ ~116-125, ν₂ 56/42, ν₃ ~125; I₅⁻: terminal I-I ~178-166, I₃⁻ units 152/118 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: GeCl₄: ν₁ 397, ν₂ 125, ν₃ 459, ν₄ 171 cm⁻¹. TiCl₄: ν₁ 389, ν₂ 114, ν₃ 498, ν₄ 136 cm⁻¹. VCl₄: ν₁ 383, ν₂ 128, ν₃ 475, ν₄ 128/150 cm⁻¹
ν(As-O-As) bridge: As₂O₇⁴⁻ νₐ ~735, νₛ ~550, δ ~245 cm⁻¹. S₂O₇²⁻ (disulfate): νₐ ~825, νₛ ~725, δ ~182/116 cm⁻¹. Systematic shift from P→As→S→Se→V→Cr
rules.spectral_details: As₂O₇⁴⁻: νₐ 735, νₛ 550, δ 245; S₂O₇²⁻: νₐ 825, νₛ 725, δ 182/116 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: N₅⁺ cation (pentanitrogen): V-shaped C2v with ν(N≡N) ~2237.6 cm⁻¹ (IR, N₂ matrix). Polymeric N₂ phase: Raman peak at 840 cm⁻¹ (cubic gauche, single N-N bonds)
rules.spectral_details: N₅⁺: ν(N≡N) 2234-2238 cm⁻¹; Polymeric N: ν(N-N) 840 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: Transuranium hexafluorides: NpF₆ ν₁ 654, ν₃ 624; PuF₆ ν₁ 656, ν₃ 616; ground and excited electronic state frequencies available. ²³⁵U/²³⁸UF₆ shift: 0.604 cm⁻¹
rules.spectral_details: UF₆: ν₁ 667, ν₃ 628; NpF₆: ν₁ 654, ν₃ 624; PuF₆: ν₁ 656, ν₃ 616 cm⁻¹

rules.rule: Os-Cl stretching in octahedral Os complexes: region 350-300 cm⁻¹. Trans-OsF₂Cl₄²⁻: ν(Os-Cl) Eu at ~325, Raman A1g+B1g at ~330-300 cm⁻¹
rules.spectral_details: Os-Cl stretch: 350-300 cm⁻¹ region. Trans: 1 IR + 2 Raman; Cis: 4 IR + 4 Raman
